name: MLGWSC gravitational-wave event search
description: search(h1, l1, metadata) -> N x 2 GPS time/ranking statistic array. Independent source observing blocks and source injections; triggers clustered and uniquely associated. Score sensitive distance at fixed FAR. At least 10 expected false alarms at the declared FAR must fit in the background duration; tiny noise clips cannot establish rare-event performance.

papers.title: Detecting and denoising gravitational wave signals from binary black holes using deep learning
papers.task_relation: The local event search uses MLGWSC source blocks and a sensitive-distance objective at fixed false-alarm rate. It pursues the same detection problem but uses a different data selection, search interface, and scoring protocol from this paper.
papers.primary_goal: Develop a detection and denoising method for binary-black-hole gravitational waves and test recovery of observed signals.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Detect gravitational waves from merging binary black holes in noisy interferometer observations.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Recovering astrophysical merger signals from detector noise is the paper's central physical detection problem.
science_relevance.reason: The evidence is a domain-specific attempt to recover physical signals, not merely the announcement of a challenge dataset.
